title: NEB Class 12 English — Writing Skills — 2022
origin: curated NEB-pattern set for class-12 English writing skills

questions.solution: Model answer: 'Reading books is one of the most rewarding habits a student can develop. First, books expand vocabulary and strengthen language skills far better than short social-media posts, because they expose readers to varied sentence structures. Second, reading improves concentration and critical thinking: following a long argument trains the mind to analyse rather than merely react. Finally, books build empathy by letting readers live lives very different from their own. In short, regular reading sharpens the mind, enriches expression and widens one's view of the world — benefits no shortcut can replace.' Check: topic sentence opens, three supports follow, conclusion closes.
questions.question: Write a paragraph of about 150 words on 'The Importance of Reading Books', with a clear topic sentence, supporting details and a concluding sentence.

questions.solution: Formal letters to unknown recipients open with 'Dear Sir/Madam,' and close with 'Yours faithfully,' (or 'Yours sincerely,' when the name is known). Options (a) and (c) are informal and only suit personal letters or messages.
questions.question: Which of these is the correct format for the salutation and closing of a FORMAL letter? (a) 'Hi Sita,' … 'Bye' (b) 'Dear Sir/Madam,' … 'Yours faithfully,' (c) 'Hey there,' … 'Cheers'

questions.solution: Layout: sender's address and date at the top; receiver's designation and address; subject line ('Subject: Request for a character certificate'); salutation ('Dear Sir/Madam,'); body in 2–3 short paragraphs — (1) self-introduction: name, class 12, roll no.; (2) reason: applying for a scholarship/job requiring the certificate; (3) polite request and thanks; closing ('Yours obediently,') with signature, name and roll number. Keep language respectful and factual — no slang, no contractions.
questions.question: Draft a formal letter to the principal of your college requesting a character certificate, giving your name, class, roll number and the reason for the request.

questions.solution:
Thesis: Social media is a powerful tool whose value depends on disciplined use — a boon for connection and learning, a bane when it controls attention.
Point 1 — Connection: reunites distant families and enables study groups across cities (e.g. exam-preparation communities).
Point 2 — Knowledge: free tutorials and news reach villages that lack libraries.
Point 3 — Harm: addictive design and comparison culture damage focus and self-esteem (e.g. falling grades linked to late-night scrolling).
Conclusion: regulate use — fixed hours, purposeful follows — and the boon outweighs the bane.
questions.question: Write an essay outline (thesis + three main points with one supporting detail each) on 'Social Media: Boon or Bane?'
